**False sharing is a hardware collision between logically independent writes.** Two workers may update different counters that happen to occupy the same CPU cache line. Cache coherence transfers ownership of the whole line, so the workers repeatedly invalidate each other's copies even though they never intentionally share a variable. [1](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/)

For example, worker A increments one progress counter while worker B increments its neighboring counter millions of times. Padding the counters onto separate lines or aggregating counts locally can reduce coherence traffic. Padding every structure indiscriminately wastes memory; first establish that frequent writes to shared lines are a meaningful cost.

**NUMA is about where memory physically lives.** On a multi-socket machine, memory attached to the local CPU socket is generally cheaper to access than memory reached through another socket's interconnect. A preprocessing worker on one socket feeding a GPU attached to another may create avoidable remote traffic. Allocation placement matters as well as CPU affinity.

Inspect CPU/GPU topology and measure locality, bandwidth, and worker stalls. Bind workers and allocate buffers near their consuming GPU when the evidence supports it. False sharing and NUMA misalignment are distinct: one is cache-line ownership contention, the other is remote-memory access. Both can leave GPUs hungry even when aggregate CPU utilization looks high, but neither explains every slow input pipeline.

**Technical details and references.**

False sharing occurs when independent CPU threads/processes update values on the same cache line, forcing coherence traffic despite no logical data sharing. Pad or partition frequently written counters and use local aggregation to reduce it. [1](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/)

NUMA means memory access cost depends on which CPU socket owns the memory. A worker on one socket reading memory allocated on another, or feeding a GPU attached to the other socket, can traverse slower interconnects. Bind workers and allocate buffers near the relevant CPU/GPU when profiling justifies it.

Distinguish cache-coherence traffic from ordinary bandwidth saturation, disk delay, or Python overhead. Measure CPU affinity, memory locality, PCIe topology, and GPU starvation. More workers can worsen throughput if they contend for remote memory or the same storage path.
